messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
**Largest “planet” known so far** | Property | Value | Notes | |----------|-------|-------| | **Radius** | ≈ 2.5 RJ (≈ 180 000 km) | HD 100546 b, a young gas‑giant orbiting a 10‑million‑year‑old star in the constellation Musca. It is the largest planet by *size* that has been confirmed. | | **Mass** | ≈ 10–12 MJ | This places it right at the boundary between massive planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs. Some authors classify it as a “super‑Jupiter” rather than a true planet. | | **Other candidates** |
  • HD 106906 b – ≈ 11 MJ, ≈ 1.5 RJ (borderline brown dwarf)
  • WASP‑17b – ≈ 0.5 MJ, ≈ 1.8 RJ (inflated, but not the largest by radius)
| These objects are close contenders, but none exceeds HD 100546 b in radius. | ### Why the distinction matters - **Planet vs. brown dwarf**: The de‑facto boundary is usually set at ~13 MJ, the mass at which deuterium fusion can occur. HD 100546 b sits just below that, so it is still considered a planet by most astronomers. - **Inflation**: Some hot Jupiters (e.g., WASP‑17b) have very low densities and large radii, but they are still smaller than HD 100546 b. ### Bottom line As of now, **HD 100546 b** is the largest confirmed planet in the universe by radius, and it sits at the upper end of the planet–brown‑dwarf spectrum. If future observations discover a truly larger planet (or a planet that is clearly below the brown‑dwarf threshold), that record will be updated.
